usageNotes: Use this to forcibly stop a running or queued task on a specific cluster node — for example, a hung migration, backup, or vzdump job. The UPID (Unique Process ID) must be obtained from a prior task-listing call; the target node must be online and reachable. Non-owner callers require 'Sys.Modify' on '/nodes/<node>'; task owners can stop their own tasks without that privilege.

examples.summary: Stop a hung vzdump backup task on node pve1

destructiveReason: Forcibly terminates the running task process, which may leave in-progress operations (backups, migrations, snapshots) in an incomplete or inconsistent state.
tips: Retrieve the UPID first via get_nodes_node_tasks (the active-task list) or the finished-task log — it is not guessable.
Check task status with get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status before stopping; the task may have already completed.
Stopping a live migration mid-flight will keep the VM on the source node but may leave lock files; check /var/run/lock/qemu-server/ if the VM shows as locked afterward.
Returns null on success — poll the task status endpoint to confirm the process has actually exited.
